c-mx-ratio.label: Mixtures of one liquid in another
c-mx-ratio.summary: Keep track of the part that does not change (the juice, or the milk-to-water balance) and let the other part move.

c-mx-cost.label: Mixing at different prices
c-mx-cost.summary: The mean price lies between the two prices. Alligation reads the ratio off the gaps to the mean.

q-mx-add.label: Add one liquid to change the ratio
q-mx-add.summary: A mixture in a ratio; add water (or juice) until another ratio is reached.

q-mx-replace.label: Remove some mixture, replace with one liquid
q-mx-replace.summary: Some mixture is taken out and replaced by pure milk; the final ratio is known.

q-mx-profit.label: Profit or loss on a mixed lot
q-mx-profit.summary: Two lots at different costs are combined and sold at one rate.

q-mx-allig.label: Ratio or quantity from a target gain
q-mx-allig.summary: A gain % on the mix fixes the mean cost; find the ratio of the two ingredients or how much of one to add.

formulas.text: In a ratio a : b of a 𝑇-litre mixture, first liquid = 𝑇a/(a + b), second = 𝑇b/(a + b)
formulas.note: 50 L at 3 : 2 → 30 L juice and 20 L water.

formulas.text: After removing x of T and replacing: the unchanged liquid's amount = original × (1 − x/T)
formulas.note: Water 10 → 5 means the mixture was thinned to half: (1 − x/80) = 1/2.
The mean is the cost price of the mix, not the selling price.

formulas.text: Cost of a mix = (q₁c₁ + q₂c₂) ÷ (q₁ + q₂)     Cost price from gain g%: CP = SP ÷ (1 + g/100)
formulas.note: Selling at ₹54 with 20% gain means CP = ₹45.

q-mx-add.cue: 'How much water must be added to change the ratio of … to …?'
q-mx-add.standard: Juice = 30 L stays. New ratio juice : water = 3 : 4 → water = 40 L. Added = 40 − 20 = 20 L.
q-mx-add.fast: Keep the unchanged part fixed: 30 L is 3 parts, so 1 part = 10 L and 4 parts = 40 L of water.
q-mx-add.eliminate: The new water is 40 L and the old was 20 L, so the answer is exactly the old water amount here (20). Any answer below 20 would leave the ratio too small.
traps: Using the total 50 as one of the parts.

q-mx-replace.cue: 'Some quantity is removed and replaced with pure …; the new ratio is …'.
q-mx-replace.standard: Water = 80 × 1/8 = 10 L. Final water is 1/16 of 80 = 5 L. Water halved, so half the mixture was replaced: 40 L.
q-mx-replace.fast: Follow the liquid that is not added (water): it falls from 10 to 5, i.e. by half. So half of the 80 L was replaced.
q-mx-replace.eliminate: Replaced amount x must satisfy 10 × (1 − x/80) = 5, so x is a whole fraction of 80. Of the options only 40 (1/2) gives a clean halving.
traps: Following the milk instead of the water.
Taking the difference 15 − 7 = 8 as the answer.
Using the ratio parts as litres.

q-mx-profit.cue: 'She bought … litres at ₹… and … litres at ₹…, mixed them and sold at ₹…. Profit or loss?'
q-mx-profit.fast: Mean cost = ₹52 a litre; selling at ₹54 gains ₹2 on each of 50 litres = ₹100.
q-mx-profit.eliminate: Mean cost lies between 50 and 55 (closer to 50), about ₹52. Selling at ₹54 is above that, so it is a profit: both 'Loss' options go.
traps: Using the simple average (50 + 55) ÷ 2 = 52.5 as the cost.

q-mx-allig.cue: 'Sold at ₹… gaining …% … what ratio / how many kg?'
q-mx-allig.standard: Spices at 80 and 160, sold at 140 with 25% profit: mean cost = 140 ÷ 1.25 = 112. Cheaper : dearer = (160 − 112) : (112 − 80) = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2. Wheat at 52 with 30 kg at 40, sold at 54 with 20% gain: mean = 45. 52x + 1,200 = 45(x + 30) gives x = 150/7 ≈ 21.4 kg.
q-mx-allig.fast: Alligation on the mean cost: the gap to the dearer one is the quantity of the cheaper one. Mean 112: gaps 48 (to 160) and 32 (to 80) → 3 : 2.
q-mx-allig.eliminate: The mean cost 112 is nearer ₹80 (gap 32) than ₹160 (gap 48), so the cheaper spice is the bigger share and the ratio cheaper : dearer is above 1 : 1. That removes 1 : 2.
traps: Using the selling price 140 as the mean (gives 3 : 1).
Reading the ratio the wrong way round.
Dropping the gain % and taking the selling price as the cost.

pyqs.text: A 50-litre mixture contains juice and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How much water (in litres) must be added to change the ratio of juice to water to 3 : 4?
solution: Juice stays 30 L. For 3 : 4 the water must be 30 × 4/3 = 40 L.
pyqs.trick: Juice is 3 parts = 30 L, so a part is 10 L; 4 parts of water = 40 L, minus the 20 L already there.

a.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (d) 20 litres.

b.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (d) 20 litres.

c.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (d) 20 litres.

pyqs.text: Priya bought 30 litres of honey at ₹50 a litre and 20 litres at ₹55 a litre, mixed them and sold all of it at ₹54 a litre. What was her total profit or loss?
pyqs.trick: The mix costs about ₹52 a litre, so selling at ₹54 is a profit. Both loss options go.

c.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (b) Profit of ₹100.

a.note: The mean cost is ₹52, below the selling price ₹54, so this is a profit, not a loss.

d.note: The mean cost is ₹52, below the selling price ₹54, so this is a profit, not a loss.

pyqs.text: Two spices priced at ₹80 and ₹160 a kg are blended and sold at ₹140 a kg, making a 25% profit. In what ratio were the spices mixed?
solution: Cost price of the mix = 140 ÷ 1.25 = ₹112 a kg.
pyqs.trick: Mean cost 112 is nearer 80, so more of the cheaper spice: ratio above 1.

b.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (a) 3:2.

d.note: Used the selling price ₹140 as the mean: (140 − 80) : (160 − 140) = 3 : 1.

c.note: The mean cost ₹112 is nearer the cheaper spice, so there is more of it: the ratio cheaper : dearer is above 1.

pyqs.text: An 80-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 1. Some of it is removed and replaced with pure milk, and the milk-to-water ratio becomes 15 : 1. How many litres of the mixture were replaced?
solution: Water = 80 ÷ 8 = 10 L. In the final mixture water is 1/16 of 80 = 5 L.
Water fell to half, so half of the mixture was removed.
pyqs.trick: Follow the water, since only milk is added: 10 L → 5 L, so exactly half was replaced.

b.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (a) 40 litres.

c.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (a) 40 litres.

d.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (a) 40 litres.

pyqs.text: How many kilograms of wheat costing ₹52 a kg must be mixed with 30 kg of wheat costing ₹40 a kg so that a 20% gain is made by selling the mixture at ₹54 a kg?
solution: Cost price of the mix = 54 ÷ 1.2 = ₹45 a kg.
pyqs.trick: Alligation on 45: the dearer wheat is ₹7 above the mean, the cheaper ₹5 below. Quantities are in the ratio 5 : 7 (dearer : cheaper)… so x = 30 × 5/7 ≈ 21.4.
